failure_patterns.pattern: answer_format: Answers were lexically close but had the wrong boundary: an unnecessary category word or suffix, a missing distinguishing numeral, or a related synonym instead of the directly matching term.

rejected_edits.content:
For proper names and titles, use the conventional form that identifies the requested entity. Do not substitute a nickname or later brand name for the historically relevant label, omit words from a work's title when the work is requested, or add optional middle names. Conversely, when the clue requests a generic class, do not embellish it with a narrower associated name.

For definition clues, prefer the directly matching headword explicitly glossed in context over a related or more specialized term from an adjacent passage. Preserve the answer boundary: when asked for a nickname, epithet, or designation itself, do not append the entity's generic class noun or repeat a category word already supplied by the clue. Retain qualifiers, such as a numeral, when they are integral to the requested conventional name.

## Check for Shared Completions in Parallel Clues
When a clue presents alternatives or examples in parallel, check whether one word completes or classifies them both. The target may be that shared word rather than a full phrase inferred from just one part of the clue. Return the minimal shared completion unless the clue asks for a full phrase.

Distinguish the shared subject category from a title of a collection that features examples: when the clue asks what the examples are, answer their category, not the collection title. Conversely, a list of people or characters can identify their common work; if context explicitly links them to that work, return it rather than a broad description of the people. Do not infer either relation from a list alone.
